items.title: Retirements turned into a 'prison' as insurance costs skyrocket
items.description: The Australian retirement dream is being destabilised by the rising cost of home insurance, as retirees on fixed budgets find themselves unable to absorb skyrocketing premiums.

items.title: There's still room for this war to get far worse. Here's what you should know now
items.description: The ABC's Middle East correspondent Matthew Doran is in Beirut and is providing daily updates on the Middle East war.

items.title: Live: Iran threatens to 'completely close' Strait of Hormuz over Trump power plant threat
items.description: Tehran says it is prepared to completely shut down the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping route for a large portion of the world's oil, if US President Donald Trump follows through on his vow to "obliterate" them.

items.title: Iran war's damage to economy could worsen yet markets remain complacent
items.description: The markets' benign assessment of the Iran war is wrong and the damage to the global economy could get worse.

items.title: Home building costs soaring 'like COVID again' on Middle East supply shocks
items.description: From sand to concrete, suppliers are bringing in "emergency fuel levies" as petrol prices soar due to the war in the Middle East. Major companies that supply pipes for plumbing are even warning of shortages.

items.title: Conditions are ripe for a party of grievance like One Nation to keep growing
items.description: One Nation delivers its best electoral result in nearly 30 years, demonstrating that opinion polls showing its vote rising was not a political beat-up but a real electoral phenomenon that will lead to a political reckoning in Australian politics.

items.title: Ghanim lost his family, then his arms. It took 12 years to make it right
items.description: Ghanim Al Shnen became a pioneer in the use of mind-controlled robotic limbs after losing both his arms. Although he would never have chosen this fate, it ultimately gave him the life for which he longed.

items.title: Agency warned of 'severe economic impact' months before fuel crisis
items.description: Nine months before the Iran war oil crisis, the federal government was warned of the "fragility" of Australia's critical infrastructure if a fuel crisis took hold.

items.title: New research finds Australians increasingly anxious about national security
items.description: Threats like economic shocks and cyber attacks were considered most likely, but nearly half of Australians expect foreign military action on Australian soil.

items.title: This 14yo is her 'family's breadwinner' — but she's about to lose her income
items.description: In a country with 70 million children, some question how the incoming social media ban in Indonesia will be effectively implemented, while others welcome the new restrictions.

items.title: Few leaders in Australia are as firmly entrenched in power than Peter Malinauskas
items.description: After Saturday's landslide, Premier Peter Malinauskas has more political capital than any South Australian Labor leader in modern history.

items.title: Are private health insurers trying to move Australia to a US-style model?
items.description: Health insurers increasingly partnering with GP centres and telehealth services has raised concerns that it could create a two-tier system in which privately insured patients have more affordable access to GP consults.

items.title: Matildas need a grand plan to stave off end-of-an-era concerns
items.description: The Women's Asian Cup has shown that without a grand plan for the future of women's football and a willingness to stick to it, the Matildas may never capture an elusive major trophy again.

items.title: Field hospital set up in Katherine as NT braces for ex-Cylone Narelle
items.description: The Northern Territory is preparing for strong gusts and drenching rain as ex-Tropical Cyclone Narelle moves further into the Top End.

items.title: The most viewed photograph in history turns 30. Here's how Bill Gates was involved
items.description: Plastered across screens in offices, schools and homes globally, Bliss is one of the most well-known images in the world.

items.title: From trees to barking dogs, here's how to resolve issues with neighbours
items.description: Someone feeling like their neighbour is intruding on them in "either psychological or practical ways" tends to be at the heart of most disputes. So if you're having an issue with the people next door, what's the best way to approach it?

items.title: Quiz: From an Oscars slap to 'sandpapergate', do you know your history?
items.description: Can you remember who Will Smith slapped, or what happened during "sandpapergate" scandal? Test yourself with today's quiz.

items.title: How councils coerce homeless people into eviction
items.description: A recent Supreme Court case has shed light on how councils coerce homeless people into eviction.

items.title: Live: ASX set to tumble after another brutal night on Wall Street, oil keeps rising
items.description: The prospect of the Middle East war dragging on led Wall Street to fall sharply and oil prices keep rising. The ASX is poised for another sell-off today. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Cheryl Grimmer's UK cousin prompts authorities to reconsider cold case
items.description: Michael Grimmer challenges the 2019 court ruling that excluded a key confession in his cousin Cheryl Grimmer's 1970 disappearance, leading to a major breakthrough in the case.

items.title: Cattle ships have an hour to navigate this channel or run aground
items.description: David Harris's ship bottomed out with 400 cattle on board at the end of last year, leading to a 12-hour wait for the next high tide. He wants a solution.

items.title: Trump orders ICE agents to man US airport security queues
items.description: A fight over funding for the Department of Homeland Security leads to lengthy queues at US airports.

items.title: Banned NDIS provider filmed entering disability housing
items.description: A man banned from working in the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) and having any contact with the program’s participants has been filmed entering specialist disability housing in Melbourne.

items.title: Australia facing 'crunch time' as oil shortages begin to hit Asian suppliers
items.description: Australia is yet to directly feel the impact of supply shortages caused by the Iran war. But that's set to change in the coming weeks, with oil supply shortages now hitting the country's fuel suppliers in Asia.

items.title: Where Australians are spending their money
items.description: As the cost-of-living crisis intensifies, people from all walks of life are struggling. ABC Your Say asked ordinary Australians how they were making ends meet.
